en: The Sūtra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Vimalamati Regarding the Paying of Homage to the Buddha-Dharma, translated by the Tripitaka Master Nadi of the Great Tang:
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in the city of Śrāvastī, in the Forest of Supreme Virtue.
In the Jeta Grove at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, the Buddha was together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus and an incalculable number of bodhisattvas.

Furthermore, he was joined by immeasurable numbers of brāhmaṇas, vaiśyas, śūdras, and various elders, each of whom was a leader of a great multitude, who had come to the place where the Buddha was together with their respective peers.
Furthermore, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas were present at the great assembly, surrounding him from front and back.

At that time, there was among the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Vimalamati. He rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms in reverence, and stepped forward to address the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"I wish to ask a few questions; I pray that you will grant me your permission.
The Buddha said, "Ask whatever you wish; I shall answer according to your inclination."
Having heard the Buddha’s permission, the Bodhisattva Vimalamati was filled with immeasurable joy and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“If there are sons or daughters of good family who, in the presence of the Tathāgata, wish to show reverence, prostrate, and make offerings, how should they do so?”
The Buddha said: “Vimalamati! Excellent, excellent!”
"You have shown great compassion, benefit, and peace for all humans and devas.
Listen attentively and well, and I shall explain it for you.
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family wishes to perform prostrations and pay homage before the Buddha, they should first make a vow, speaking these words: "
"I now, with a sincere heart, pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions and universally enter into all supreme dharmas.

I now prostrate to the Buddha with my five limbs to sever the five paths, to depart from the five hindrances, and to vow that all sentient beings shall always abide in peace, never lose the five supernormal powers, and be fully endowed with the five eyes."
When my right knee touches the ground, may all sentient beings attain the path of perfect enlightenment.

When my left knee touches the ground, may all sentient beings not give rise to false views regarding the teachings of non-Buddhist paths, and may they all be firmly established upon the path of perfect enlightenment.

"May it be that when my right hand touches the earth, just as the World-Honored One sat upon the Vajra Seat and pointed to the ground with his right hand, causing the earth to tremble and manifest auspicious omens as he realized Great Bodhi—so may it be for me now; together with all sentient beings, may we equally realize the Way of Enlightenment."
When my left hand touches the ground, may all those heterodox practitioners who are difficult to subdue be gathered through the four means of attraction and led to enter the True Dharma.
"May it be that when my head touches the ground, all sentient beings shall be freed from the mind of pride and fully attain the mark of the invisible crown of the head.
Thus spoke Vigatamala-prajñā.
This is the manner of performing the five-point prostration.
Next, one should pay homage to all the Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions, speaking these words:
"Namo to the Tathāgata Akṣobhya of the East."

Extensively reaching all Tathāgatas, the great treasuries of Dharma, as well as all Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all worthy sages throughout the immeasurable worlds of those directions.
“Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnākara of the southern quarter.

I also pay homage extensively to all the Tathāgatas in the infinite worlds of that direction, to all the great Dharma-treasuries, and to all the worthy and holy ones—Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.”
“Homage to the Tathāgata Amitāyus of the western quarter.
Extensively, [homage] to all the Tathāgatas of the infinite worlds in that direction, to the great Dharma-treasuries, and to all the bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all worthy sages.”
“Homage to the Tathāgata Sublime Drum Sound of the North.
Extensively, [homage] to all the Tathāgatas in the infinite worlds of that direction, to all the great Dharma treasuries, and to all the worthy sages—Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.”
“Homage to the Tathāgata Indra-ketu-dhvaja-rāja in the southeast.

I pay homage extensively to all the Tathāgatas, the great Dharma-treasuries, as well as all the Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all the worthy sages throughout the immeasurable worlds of that direction.”
“Homage to the Tathāgata Ratnavikrāmin of the southwest.

I pay homage extensively to all the Tathāgatas, the great Dharma-treasuries, as well as all the Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all the worthy sages of the infinite worlds in that direction.”
“Namo to the Tathāgata Śaraindrarāja of the northwest, and extensively to all the Tathāgatas,
the great Dharma-treasuries, as well as all the Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all worthy sages of the infinite worlds in that direction.”
“Homage to the Tathāgata Immeasurable Banner King of the Northeast.

I pay homage extensively to all the Tathāgatas, the great Dharma treasuries, as well as all the Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all the worthy and holy ones of the immeasurable worlds in that direction.”
“Homage to the Tathāgata Jñānaprabha of the upper direction.

I pay homage extensively to all the Tathāgatas in all the immeasurable worlds of that direction, to all the great treasuries of the Dharma, and to all the worthy and holy ones—Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas.”
“Homage to the Tathāgata Vairocana of the lower direction,
extensively including all Tathāgatas in the infinite worlds of that direction, the great Dharma-treasuries, as well as all Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and all worthy sages.”
"Next, I again take refuge in the Original Teacher of the Sahā World, Śākyamuni Tathāgata;

extensively including all Tathāgatas of the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions, all the great Dharma-treasuries, and all the worthy sages, such as Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have entered the stages, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas."
"Furthermore, he spoke these words:
'I now single-mindedly prostrate to all the Buddhas, Dharmas, and the assembly of worthy sages as described above; may they bear witness to me.'"

From this day forth until I attain enlightenment, I shall always practice taking refuge in the Buddha, the World-Honored One, the Greatly Compassionate One, the Omniscient One, the One Possessed of All Knowledge and Vision, the One Who Has Transcended All Fears, the Great Lion among Men, the Great Dragon King, the Great Sage among Men, the Great Being, the All-Pervading Knower, whose body is inconceivable, supreme, peerless, not shared with the two vehicles, and which is the pure Dharma-body—the most honored and exalted among all assemblies. With utmost sincerity and single-minded devotion, I now take refuge in him.

Thus, one takes refuge a hundred times, a thousand times, a hundred thousand times, even up to immeasurable and incalculable times, until the end of the future, reaching to the very marrow of one's bones, taking refuge in the aforementioned Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
Furthermore, they speak thus:
"By means of the roots of goodness from my current actions of body, speech, and mind, together with all sentient beings, I take refuge in the Buddha and shall never be separated from him."

I now, with utmost sincerity, earnestness, and gravity, take refuge in the True Dharma of all such Buddhas: those who have returned to the seat of enlightenment; who are eternally abiding, perpetual, and immutable; who do not age, do not die, and are not subject to destruction; who are without dwelling and without objects of perception, being by nature quiescent; who dwell in the abode of Dharma and provide great protective mindfulness as an island of refuge; who serve as the resort and reliance for realizing nirvana; and who abide in the most supreme state among all dharmas.

Again, as before, with utmost sincerity, I take refuge in all those bodhisattvas dwelling within the lineage, from the Stage of Joy up to the Cloud of Dharma—those members of the Bodhisattva Saṃgha who abide in the ten stages.
"Next, one should perform confession, speaking these words:
'I only pray that the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions will bear witness, keep me in mind, and compassionately accept my confession.'"
The three types of physical karma consist of killing, stealing, and sexual misconduct;
the four types of verbal karma consist of lying, harsh speech, divisive speech, and frivolous chatter;
and the three types of mental karma consist of greed, hatred, and delusion.
"Whatever I have committed myself, caused others to commit, or rejoiced in seeing others commit—these ten unwholesome deeds, I now repent of them all.
Furthermore, he reflects again:
"Since beginningless time, as I have transmigrated through the six realms, I have oppressed and deceived sentient beings in manifold ways."

I used oversized scoops and heavy scales to take goods for my own profit, while giving others smaller measures and light scales; I feigned ornaments on my clothes and secretly administered poisons—all such acts were intended to cause harm, and I now repent them all.

Some slander the Three Vehicles and falsely expound the Dharma and Vinaya; they treat the Triple Gem with contempt, deceive their parents, and fail to show reverence before their elders, preceptors (upādhyāya), instructors (ācārya), and the aged.
All such past transgressions as these, I now fully repent;
my present evil karma, I confess with a sincere heart;
and as for those yet to be committed, I dare not do them again.

Now, before all the Buddhas, the great leaders of the assembly of Bodhisattvas, and those who are peerless, unsurpassed, and unequaled, I openly confess and repent, not daring to conceal anything; having confessed once, I shall never again commit such acts.
Having thus repented, the second and third times should also be performed as described above.
Next, one should make the request for exhortation, speaking these words:

"O Buddhas of the ten directions, whether you have not yet turned the wheel of Dharma, or intend to enter parinirvāṇa, I entreat you all: I pray that you remain for a long time; out of compassion for all sentient beings throughout immeasurable kalpas, rain down the great rain of Dharma, turn the true wheel of Dharma, and do not pass into parinirvāṇa."
"Next, one should express sympathetic joy (*anumodana*), speaking these words:

'I rejoice in all the holy ones of the three vehicles throughout the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, as well as in all sentient beings who practice the six perfections and the dharmas that assist enlightenment.'"
"Next, one should perform dedication, speaking these words:

'The deeds performed by all Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, as well as the practice of the six perfections by all Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, and Pratyekabuddhas, have all been dedicated toward unsurpassed bodhi; I likewise dedicate [my merit] toward the Buddha-way.'"
"Next, one should make this vow:

'I look up to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions and the three periods of time, who have all made great vows to manifest their transformative activities throughout the entirety of empty space and the pervasiveness of the Dharma-realm for the sake of all sentient beings, leaving none among those encompassed by the three realms behind. I vow that these beings shall be brought to benefit, joy, and maturity; that they shall be endowed with virtuous discipline; and that they shall abide in Great Nirvana—may all of these now be manifested before me.'"

I too am thus adorned with this great vow: may my mind remain undistracted from the unsurpassed path; may I constantly behold all Buddhas and constantly hear the True Dharma; may I serve and practice it without any passing in vain;
may the wholesome dharmas I perform and my bodhicitta never decline or be lost;

and in every place where I am born, may I make offerings to the assembly of sages, transform sentient beings, attain the unsurpassed path, turn the wheel of the True Dharma, and possess great supernormal powers.
I also cause sentient beings to practice and study in this way until they reach the stage of non-retrogression.
"Furthermore, I vow that all sentient beings shall quickly sever all sufferings, swiftly realize nirvana, and abide in the wisdom of the Tathāgata."

Since I have emerged from birth and death and awakened to all things, I shall likewise cause all sentient beings to transcend birth and death, liberate them from afflictions, and awaken them to all things.
"I only pray that the Buddhas of the ten directions will bear witness to my practice of the bodhisattva path and my arousal of the ocean of vows.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke again in verse:
"May I, in whatever place I am born, Receive a physical form according to my karma;..."
He has attained the body of a great man, endowed with faith and all the faculties.
Proficient in arts, crafts, and skills, he has extensively understood the meaning of all teachings;
having utterly renounced worldly affairs, he remains far removed from all desires.
Abiding in right speech with mindfulness of the Dharma, adorning the bodhicitta,
and reverently serving spiritual friends, one is held in high esteem by all sentient beings.
With the precepts and conduct fully perfected, one receives the joyful retribution of pure mindfulness.
Constantly fearing those evil karmas, he walks within the wholesome Dharma;
always relying on the practice of the ten perfections, he thus attains Bodhi.
Even unto his final body, he constantly bestows happiness upon all sentient beings.
"The maṇi among jewels is supreme; it can accomplish the welfare of others.
May I, until the end of the future, benefit beings without ceasing.
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vigatamala-prajñā, saying:
"If there are sentient beings who practice the bodhisattva path, they should rely upon and train according to what I have taught.

When this sutra had been spoken, Vimalamati and the rest of the great assembly—including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
The Sūtra on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Vimalamati Concerning the Paying of Homage to the Buddha-Dharma.
